content.text:
Make a 3D model that, if everyone saw it, would improve the world for the greatest number of people.

Make it in Blender, working in the current directory.
- A Blender 5 instance is running for you with no window (background mode). Use it through the `blender`
  MCP tools: run Python (`bpy`) with execute_blender_code, and look things up with the API and manual
  search tools. Blender's working directory is the current directory. The scene starts as Blender's
  default one (a cube, a camera and a light).
- There is no window to screenshot. To check your work, render it to an image file and look at the image
  (render_thumbnail_to_path, render_viewport_to_path, or a render of the scene camera to a file).
  Keep renders quick: a single tool call may take at most 5 minutes. Save what you look at as .jpg rather
  than .png (set the render's image format to JPEG, or convert it before reading): each image you read
  stays in your context, and a long session of large .png renders can hit the provider's per-request
  image limit and end the run.
- Build it in Blender itself; don't write the model or the images any other way.
- Save the finished result in ./output/ (only what is in ./output/ is published):
  - the model or scene as one .glb file (glTF binary), shown on the site in an interactive 3D viewer:
    `bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=..., export_format='GLB')`, without Draco or meshopt
    compression, at most 15 MB;
  - one or more final renders as .png or .jpg, at most 2 MB each, from camera angles you choose.
  At most 8 files in all.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.12.13 (standard library only), node 24.18.0 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 8.1.1, ffprobe 8.1.1. Don't install packages or download anything (no asset
  libraries or add-ons).
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

I’m making a small monument to shared care: many different hands supporting one living world, with an open place for the viewer to join. I’ll build it in Blender and check rendered views before exporting.

content.text: The sculpture will pair a globe and new growth with five distinct hands. I’m giving the materials a ceramic-and-brass finish, and using the inscription “No one thrives alone” to make the idea of mutual care explicit.

import bpy, math, os
from mathutils import Vector
bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)
root=os.getcwd(); os.makedirs(os.path.join(root,'output'),exist_ok=True)
scene=bpy.context.scene
scene.render.engine='CYCLES'; scene.cycles.samples=32
scene.cycles.use_denoising=True
scene.render.resolution_x=1100; scene.render.resolution_y=1250; scene.render.resolution_percentage=100
scene.render.image_settings.file_format='JPEG'; scene.render.image_settings.quality=90
scene.world.color=(0.15,0.15,0.15)
world=scene.world; world.use_nodes=True; world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs[0].default_value=(0.15,0.21,0.25,1); world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs[1].default_value=.35
scene.view_settings.view_transform='AgX'

def mat(name,color,metal=0,rough=.4):
 m=bpy.data.materials.new(name); m.diffuse_color=(*color,1); m.use_nodes=True
 p=m.node_tree.nodes.get('Principled BSDF'); p.inputs['Base Color'].default_value=(*color,1); p.inputs['Metallic'].default_value=metal; p.inputs['Roughness'].default_value=rough
 return m
mats={}
mats['base']=mat('Midnight | glazed stone',(.022,.052,.064),.2,.27)
mats['gold']=mat('Brushed champagne brass',(.67,.43,.16),.72,.28)
mats['ocean']=mat('Ocean | deep petrol enamel',(.016,.16,.20),.3,.23)
mats['land']=mat('Land | celadon porcelain',(.39,.65,.48),.12,.35)
mats['grid']=mat('Quiet cartographic lines',(.055,.26,.29),.35,.35)
mats['leaf']=mat('New growth | malachite',(.045,.28,.12),.12,.34)
mats['vein']=mat('Leaf midrib | spring green',(.38,.58,.17),.15,.4)
mats['floor']=mat('Warm gallery plaster',(.67,.63,.54),0,.76)
clays=[(.65,.36,.20),(.25,.12,.075),(.78,.60,.40),(.43,.23,.14),(.9,.75,.56)]
for i,c in enumerate(clays): mats['hand'+str(i)]=mat('Fired earth | hand '+str(i+1),c,.07,.4)
def assign(o,m): o.data.materials.append(m); return o
def smooth(o):
 if o.type=='MESH':
  for p in o.data.polygons: p.use_smooth=True
 return o
def sphere(name,loc,scale,ma,seg=32,rings=20):
 bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(segments=seg,ring_count=rings,location=loc); o=bpy.context.object; o.name=name; o.scale=scale; assign(o,ma); smooth(o); return o
def cyl(name,rad,depth,z,ma):
 bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=128,radius=rad,depth=depth,location=(0,0,z)); o=bpy.context.object; o.name=name; assign(o,ma)
 b=o.modifiers.new('Soft machined edge','BEVEL'); b.width=.055; b.segments=3
 o.modifiers.new('Weighted normals','WEIGHTED_NORMAL'); return o
def path(name,pts,radius,ma,cyclic=False):
 cu=bpy.data.curves.new(name,'CURVE'); cu.dimensions='3D'; cu.resolution_u=16; cu.bevel_depth=radius; cu.bevel_resolution=3
 sp=cu.splines.new('POLY'); sp.points.add(len(pts)-1)
 for p,co in zip(sp.points,pts): p.co=(*co,1)
 sp.use_cyclic_u=cyclic; ob=bpy.data.objects.new(name,cu); scene.collection.objects.link(ob); assign(ob,ma); return ob
cyl('01 | foundation',2.5,.22,.11,mats['base'])
cyl('Brass reveal',2.42,.055,.245,mats['gold'])
cyl('02 | common ground',2.37,.24,.385,mats['base'])
# Fine inlaid perimeter, open on the viewer side
for rr in [2.15,2.22]:
 pts=[(rr*math.cos(a),rr*math.sin(a),.512) for a in [math.radians(-53+j*286/220) for j in range(221)]]
 path('Open circle | room for you',pts,.009,mats['gold'])
# Globe
C=Vector((0,0,3.65)); R=1.35
sphere('03 | our only home',C,(R,R,R),mats['ocean'],96,64)
def globe(lon,lat,r=R+.006):
 lo=math.radians(lon); la=math.radians(lat)
 return (r*math.cos(la)*math.sin(lo),-r*math.cos(la)*math.cos(lo),3.65+r*math.sin(la))
for lat in [-60,-30,0,30,60]: path('Latitude '+str(lat),[globe(i,lat) for i in range(-180,180,2)],.004,mats['grid'],True)
for lon in range(0,180,30):
 pts=[globe(lon,j) for j in range(-90,91,2)]+[globe(lon+180,j) for j in range(90,-91,-2)]
 path('Meridian '+str(lon),pts,.004,mats['grid'],True)
result={'setup':'complete','materials':len(bpy.data.materials)}

/bin/zsh -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import struct,json
p=Path('output/common-ground.glb')
b=p.read_bytes()
magic,version,length=struct.unpack_from('<4sII',b)
jslen,jstype=struct.unpack_from('<II',b,12)
g=json.loads(b[20:20+jslen])
assert magic==b'glTF' and version==2 and length==len(b)
assert not any(x in g.get('extensionsUsed',[]) for x in ['KHR_draco_mesh_compression','EXT_meshopt_compression'])
assert all('uri' not in buffer for buffer in g['buffers'])
assert len(b)<15_000_000
files=list(Path('output').iterdir())
assert len(files)==3
for f in files:
    assert f.stat().st_size < (15_000_000 if f.suffix=='.glb' else 2_000_000)
print(json.dumps({'valid_glb':True,'meshes':len(g['meshes']),'materials':len(g['materials']),'files':{f.name:f.stat().st_size for f in files}},indent=2))
PY"

Created **Common Ground**: five ceramic hands supporting a living Earth, with an open circle inviting participation. Its inscription reads **“No one thrives alone.”**

Saved in `output/`: the 4 MB GLB model and two final JPG renders, all within the requested limits.
